rv.q: There’s hope and heartache, triumph and adversity, disco dancing and Welsh choirs — it’s the stuff of musical theatre heaven.
Writer Stephen Beresford’s musical adaptation of his own 2014 film is a triumph.
It hasn't yet found the right sound or dramatic depth to do full justice to its subject matter.
Coming to London when many Reform councils across England have banned Pride celebrations, and with trans rights in danger under the current Labour Government, this musical is vital.

Then there are the declarations of personal power: Jonathan has his fantasy moment opening Act Two, and Joe has perhaps the best line of the night (“I like c**k and Ethel Merman”). Pride is about two communities coming together against the common enemy – and yes, there is one person in the valley who hates that and tries to ruin it.
To celebrate their story so vividly and joyously is a privilege.
Instead, Matthew Warchus and Stephen Beresford, director and writer of the hit film respectively, have reunited to produce an utterly joyous and triumphant musical.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this joyous, heartbreaking musical about queer activists supporting Welsh miners, praising its galvanizing message and triumphant storytelling, though one dissenter finds it dramatically shallow.

ru.inst: Released Fridays at 1 PM via the National Theatre website (random queue).
